# Confirmed bytes and release metadata: docs/research/reference-087-d.md §5; gathered 2026-10-22.
schema_version = 1
id = "abandon"
title = "Abandon"
authors = ["Bemused", "Benjogami", "Scotty"]
release = "2023-05-07 update (original 2020 release)"
# First public release (spec 090): the 2020 Cacowards Top Ten page 1 covers the original 2020 release; the pinned 2023 archive text is a later update, and no day is evidenced. See docs/research/catalog-release-dates.md.
original_release = { year = 2020 }
page = "https://www.doomworld.com/idgames/levels/doom2/Ports/megawads/abandon"
description = "DOOM II: 17 Boom-compatible slaughter maps (MAP01–MAP17) in sombre, oppressive settings, plus a short closing map; aimed at experienced players."
permission = "Authors may NOT use the contents of this file as a base for modification or reuse; permissions were obtained from the original authors of any resources modified or included. You MAY distribute this file provided you include this text file intact and unmodified, in any electronic format. DDL downloads the unmodified archive and keeps the bundled text."
tags = ["cacowards", "challenging"]

# Bundled screenshot(s) (spec 023, D-024): the images live under
# crates/ddl/ui/assets/screenshots/abandon/ with source, credit and permission
# text in SOURCES.toml beside them; the build embeds them for card, detail and band.
[[screenshots]]
asset = "abandon/01.jpg"
credit = "Bemused, Benjogami & Scotty"

[base_game]
game = "doom2"
variants = []

[compatibility]
family = "boom"
complevel = "boom"

[compatibility.engine]
range = "=0.30.1"
status = "inspected"

[compatibility.runtime]
# Continuous DOOM II set (MAP01–MAP17 with a small ending map at MAP18); no UMAPINFO or
# MAPINFO lump, so the menu selects the map and no warp is prescribed.

[verification]
status = "inspected"
tester = "DDL desk research"
date = "2026-10-22"
engine_version = "0.30.1"
inspected = [
  "docs/research/reference-087-d.md §5.1 and §6",
  "Downloaded abandon.zip from three byte-identical mirrors; 46,212,925 bytes, SHA-256 9ef49a28…; ZIP central directory has Abandon.txt (4,997 B) and Abandon.wad (177,444,166 B)",
  "Abandon.wad: PWAD, 767 lumps, eighteen map markers MAP01–MAP18, twenty-one D_* music lumps, one embedded DEHACKED lump; no COMPLVL, UMAPINFO or MAPINFO lump. MAP01–MAP17 are the released levels and MAP18 is a four-thing ending map (DEHACKED string \"HUSTR_18 = The End\")",
  "Map-lump sizes read from the WAD directory: 167,702,999 bytes across the eighteen slots; the largest is MAP12 at 29,091,075 bytes, and MAP09/MAP10 place 8,672/10,030 things (74,510 things across all eighteen slots)",
  "Authors' Abandon.txt: Release date 05/07/2023 = 2023-05-07 (the readme writes month/day; the ZIP's Abandon.txt is dated 2023-05-07 and the WAD 2023-02-10), DOOM2, MAP01–MAP17, New levels: 17, \"Grandiose, oppressive slaughter maps.\", \"Advanced engine needed: Boom\", \"Tested With: PRBoom+ 2.4.1.5, DSDA-Doom 0.x.x\", \"May Not Run With: zDaemon as several maps use extended nodes\", Dehacked/BEX Patch: Yes, Music: Yes",
  "Cacowards 2020 Top Ten, page 1: https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2020/best1/ (page read at https://web.archive.org/web/20201210111058id_/https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2020/best1/; title \"2020 Cacowards - Top Ten Page 1 - Doomworld\")",
  "Cacowards 2020 screenshot: https://web.archive.org/web/2026id_/https://static.doomworld.com/pages_media/9_abandon.jpg?_cb=1607467020",
]
notes = "Confirmed archive and member identities from downloads on www.gamers.org, mirrors.lug.mtu.edu and ftp.fu-berlin.de that return identical size and SHA-256; nothing downloaded was extracted to disk or executed. The archive holds exactly two root members, Abandon.txt and Abandon.wad, with the case shown. The WAD embeds its DEHACKED patch (level names and intermission text), all twenty-one music lumps and its own status-bar graphics, so no separate -deh member or soundtrack package is needed. The bundled text is a 2023-05-07 update: the authors list 17 new levels MAP01–MAP17, while the WAD also carries a small MAP18 ending map; the Cacoward was awarded for the 2020 release, and this recipe pins the 2023 archive bytes rather than the award-year download. No COMPLVL lump exists: complevel boom comes from the author's \"Advanced engine needed: Boom\" line, and the same text says it was tested with DSDA-Doom. The author's \"May Not Run With: zDaemon as several maps use extended nodes\" is recorded as an author statement, not a DDL test. Inspected size facts for the performance limitation, not a measurement: 177,444,166-byte WAD, 167,702,999 bytes of map lumps, MAP12 alone 29,091,075 bytes, and 74,510 things across the map slots. Tags: cacowards = 2020 Top Ten winner, page 1; challenging = the authors describe the set as \"Grandiose, oppressive slaughter maps\" and the Cacowards entry calls its environs \"legitimately perilous\". Not tagged megawad or episode: 17 released maps is over the nine-map episode limit and under the thirty-map megawad limit, and MAP18 is an ending map rather than an eighteenth level. Not tagged classics: the pinned archive text is dated 2023-05-07, less than five years before this review, even though the project itself won in 2020. No gameplay or performance test was performed."
limitations = [
  "Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, load order, DEHACKED application, gameplay, audio, extended-node rendering and map progression.",
  "Needs Deck Validation: performance and memory use on the Steam Deck. Inspected facts only: a 177,444,166-byte WAD, 167,702,999 bytes of map lumps, a 29,091,075-byte MAP12 and up to 10,030 things in one map; no FPS, frame time, battery or thermal measurement was made.",
  "The recipe ships the 2023-05-07 archive; the 2020 Cacowards award refers to that year's release of the same project, and the earlier bytes are not pinned here.",
  "The MAP18 ending map is not described in the authors' level list; confirm that DSDA-Doom reaches and exits it as intended.",
]

The MAP31 performance warning is an explicit owner request (2026-10-21) based on the owner's knowledge, not a DDL measurement of FPS or enemy count."

inspected = ["docs/research/haste.md §1–§5", "Archive and member sizes/SHA-256; WAD lump inventory (eighteen map markers MAP01–MAP17 and MAP31, embedded DEHACKED strings, ZDoom-syntax MAPINFO); author's release text read byte-for-byte", "DSDA-Doom v0.30.1 prboom2/src/p_spec.c generalized-linedef dispatch and prboom2/src/dsda/mapinfo/ (legacy.c hardcoded progression, u.c UMAPINFO, hexen.c)"]
notes = "Confirmed package/member identities from three byte-identical mirrors and eighteen map markers: MAP01–MAP17 plus the secret MAP31. Complevel boom: the author's text states 'Advanced engine needed: Boom' and lists DSDA-Doom 0.2.3 among tested engines; 17 of the 18 maps use Boom generalized line types (390 lines: 267 floor, 71 lift, 22 door, 20 locked-door, 9 ceiling, 1 crusher), which vanilla compatibility does not implement. The MAPINFO lump is ZDoom syntax (defaultmap/map blocks with titlepatch/next/sky1/cluster/music), not a Boom format, and DSDA-Doom v0.30.1 has no ZDoom MAPINFO reader, so its titles and per-map music do not apply. With no UMAPINFO or COMPLVL, progression is the hardcoded Doom II next-map table (legacy.c): MAP17 is the author's 'Thanks for Playing' ending map, after which the run would continue into the base IWAD's MAP18 unless the player quits; the secret MAP31 returns to the base IWAD's MAP32 on a normal exit. The embedded DEHACKED relabels maps only. Dates: the readme says 22/09/2021 (day-first, unambiguous) and the idgames file is dated 2022-01-08, a later archive upload. Tags: cacowards = 2021 Top Twelve (page 4) winner, https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2021/best4/ (read through the Wayback capture of 2021-12-10); community-projects = the readme credits two project leads and seven mappers; classics = released 2021-09-22, over five years before this review, with that Cacowards recognition. Not megawad: the archive directory says megawads but the WAD and readme have eighteen slots, fewer than thirty. Not challenging: the Cacowards write-up says the set was built to be approachable to players who do not live and breathe hardcore gameplay, so no experienced-players claim is made. The owner's gimmick tag covers The 10x10 Project and Linear Doom only, so it is not applied here. Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, DEHACKED application, gameplay, audio, performance and progression."
limitations = ["Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, load order, embedded DEHACKED application, gameplay, audio and map selection.", "The ZDoom-syntax MAPINFO is inert in DSDA-Doom v0.30.1; confirm the map titles and music actually heard on the Deck.", "No UMAPINFO or COMPLVL exists. After the author's MAP17 ending map the hardcoded Doom II progression would continue into the base IWAD's MAP18, and a normal MAP31 exit leads to the base IWAD's MAP32; quit from the intermission to stop.", "Several maps use extended nodes (the author warns zDaemon cannot run them); confirm DSDA-Doom's node handling on the Deck.", "No framerate, memory or battery measurement was made; Deck performance of the compact slaughter maps is unverified.", "No separate DEHACKED member exists: the patch is embedded in Haste.wad and its hash is covered by the member identity."]

  "Cacowards 2016 Top Ten, page 3: https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2016/ (edition page read at https://web.archive.org/web/2026id_/https://www.doomworld.com/23years/best3.php; the page header reads \"Top Ten - Page 3\")",

The map WAD embeds its DEHACKED patch (level names and intermission text) and all thirty-five music lumps, so no separate -deh member or soundtrack package is needed. The archive's JPCP.txt is not valid UTF-8 (a CP932 ellipsis byte at offset 9,547); the recipe pins its exact bytes and the kept file is never edited. No COMPLVL lump exists: complevel vanilla follows D-030's limit-removing convention and agrees with the authors' own \"PrBoom+ with doom 2 compatibility (-complevel 2)\" test note, since vanilla resolves to 2 on Doom II. The ZDoom-format MAPINFO is inert in DSDA-Doom v0.30.1 (ZDoom MAPINFO support was removed in v0.30.0), so the set plays as one continuous 32-map run. Progression therefore uses the hardcoded Doom II next-map table (legacy.c): after the custom MAP05 the run continues into the base IWAD's MAP06 unless the player quits. The embedded DEHACKED edits a Keen type, frames and level names. Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, DEHACKED application, gameplay, audio and the post-MAP05 transition."
limitations = ["Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, load order, DEHACKED application, gameplay, audio and map selection.", "The ZDoom MAPINFO and Eternity EMAPINFO lumps are inert in DSDA-Doom v0.30.1; map titles and the per-map music selection fall back to engine behaviour. Confirm what plays on the Deck.", "No UMAPINFO or COMPLVL exists. The MAPINFO's MAP05 next points at MAP06 (itself missing from the PWAD); the hardcoded Doom II progression therefore loads the base IWAD's MAP06. description = "DOOM II: fifteen maps — a six-map island-hopping holiday that turns hellish, a game-over map, a harder New Game Plus run and a bonus secret map; the author describes the difficulty as average."
permission = "Licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-ND 4.0): redistribution is permitted with credit and a link to the licence, no commercial use and no distribution of modified material. DDL downloads the unmodified archive and keeps the bundled credits file."

# Bundled screenshot (spec 023, D-024): the image lives under

[base_game]

variants = []

[compatibility]

[compatibility.engine]

status = "inspected"

[compatibility.runtime]
# Single continuous DOOM II mapset (MAP01–MAP14 and MAP31, no UMAPINFO or COMPLVL).
# The menu selects the map, so no warp is prescribed.

[verification]
status = "inspected"
tester = "DDL desk research"
date = "2026-10-22"
engine_version = "0.30.1"
inspected = ["docs/research/reference-087-c.md §5", "Archive and member sizes/SHA-256; WAD lump inventory (fifteen map markers MAP01–MAP14 and MAP31, embedded DEHACKED, no MAPINFO/UMAPINFO/COMPLVL); author's release text read byte-for-byte", "DSDA-Doom v0.30.1 prboom2/src/p_spec.c generalized-linedef dispatch"]
notes = "Confirmed package/member identities from three byte-identical mirrors and the fifteen map markers MAP01–MAP14 plus MAP31. Complevel boom is the author's own statement: '6 maps of island-hopping mayhem for Doom 2 (boom format, complevel 9)', with 'Advanced engine needed: Boom' and 'May Not Run With: non-boom ports'; the maps use Boom generalized linedef types. The embedded DEHACKED changes level names, pickup text and a few frames. Progression uses DSDA-Doom's hardcoded Doom II next-map table (legacy.c): the author's 'game over' map and New Game Plus flow are ordinary custom maps, and after MAP14 the run continues into the base IWAD's MAP15 unless the player quits. Tags: cacowards = 2022 Top Ten (page 3) winner, https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2022/best3/ (read through the Wayback capture of 2022-12-10). The Cacowards blurb counts '6 maps'; the release and the WAD have fifteen slots, so the <=9-map episode tag is not claimed. Not tagged challenging: the author calls the difficulty 'average'. Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, DEHACKED application, New Game Plus flow, gameplay, audio, map selection and the post-MAP14 transition."
limitations = ["Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, load order, DEHACKED application, gameplay, audio and map selection.", "New Game Plus continues past the MAP07 'game over' map into the harder MAP08–MAP13 variants; confirm the intended transition, MAP14 'the actual end' and MAP31 on the Deck.", "No UMAPINFO or COMPLVL exists. The hardcoded Doom II progression continues from the custom MAP14 into the base IWAD's MAP15; quit from the intermission to stop after the author's ending map.", "Some maps are documented by the author as not working with -nomonsters; DDL does not pass that flag.", "No separate DEHACKED member exists: the patch is embedded in overboard.wad and its hash is covered by the member identity."]

date = "2026-10-22"
engine_version = "0.30.1"
inspected = [
  "docs/research/reference-087-d.md §4 and §5",
  "Downloaded ozonia.zip from three byte-identical mirrors; 17,180,670 bytes, SHA-256 f5bbc36e…; ZIP central directory has ozonia.txt (6,595 B, ZIP timestamp 2022-11-04) and ozonia.wad (55,559,897 B, ZIP timestamp 2022-10-30)",
  "ozonia.wad: PWAD, 1,532 lumps, thirty-two map markers MAP01–MAP32, thirty-five D_* music lumps, one embedded DEHACKED lump, one UMAPINFO lump (episode definitions) and a ZDoom-format MAPINFO; no COMPLVL lump",
  "Authors' ozonia.txt: release 23/12/2021, DOOM2, Map01–Map32, \"containing 32 carefully designed short maps with compatibility level 9\", \"Advanced engine needed: Prboom\", two new enemies, Dehacked/BEX Patch: Yes, Music: Yes",
  "Cacowards 2022 Top Ten, page 1: https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2022/best1/ (page title \"Top Ten - Page 1\"; entry \"Ozonia - @Deadwing Doom 2, Boom-compatible, 32 maps\")",
  "Cacowards 2022 screenshot: https://web.archive.org/web/2026id_/https://static.doomworld.com/pages_media/13_ozonia.png",
]
notes = "Confirmed archive and member identities from downloads on www.gamers.org, mirrors.lug.mtu.edu and ftp.fu-berlin.de that return identical size and SHA-256; nothing downloaded was extracted to disk or executed. No COMPLVL lump exists: complevel boom comes from the author's own \"compatibility level 9\" and \"Advanced engine needed: Prboom\" statements. The ZIP member timestamps (2022-10-30 WAD, 2022-11-04 text) are later than the readme's stated 2021-12-23 release date; the recipe keeps the author's stated release and pins the archived bytes by size and SHA-256. Tags: cacowards = 2022 Top Ten winner, page 1; megawad = 32 maps, MAP01–MAP32. Not tagged classics: released 2021-12-23, less than five years before this review. Not tagged challenging: the author compares the difficulty to Eviternity with a deliberate learning curve in the early maps, which is not an experienced-players-only claim. No gameplay test was performed."
limitations = [
  "Needs Deck Validation: IWAD/complevel, load order, DEHACKED application, new-enemy behaviour, gameplay, audio and episode/map selection.",
  "Needs Deck Validation: the UMAPINFO three-episode menu and intermission text under DSDA-Doom v0.30.1.",
  "The readme's map list places Penitencia at MAP32 while its credits list map 31; the recipe credits the guest mappers without asserting slot authorship.",
  "The bundled screenshot is a 1280x960 (4:3) Cacowards image, resized to 1066x800; confirm the card crop on the Deck.",
]

limitations = ["Needs Deck Validation: Plutonia IWAD selection, complevel, embedded DEHACKED application, load order, gameplay, audio and map selection.", "MAP33 'Chocolate' is defined only in the ZDoom MAPINFO lump; DSDA-Doom removed ZDoom MAPINFO support in v0.30.0, so the bonus map is not reachable without a separate UMAPINFO (not supplied by the release).", "The external PL2.DEH is deliberately not declared; confirm on the Deck that the WAD's embedded DEHACKED level names and story text appear."]

description = "A DOOM II set with ten main maps, a secret map and a no-exit finale (twelve map slots). Each main map is built from only ten stock textures and ten stock flats, and the combat ranges from Plutonia-style to Sunder-esque."
permission = "Authors may use the contents as a base for modification or reuse, and the author states permission was obtained from the original authors of any modified or included resources. Redistribution is permitted provided 10x10.txt travels with the file, unmodified and intact. DDL downloads the unmodified archive and keeps the bundled credits file."
tags = ["cacowards", "gimmick"]

[compatibility]
family = "boom"
complevel = "boom"

[compatibility.engine]
range = "=0.30.1"

[compatibility.runtime]
# Twelve map slots (MAP01–MAP11 plus MAP31) with UMAPINFO. The menu selects the map, so no warp is prescribed.
pistol_start = true

[verification]
status = "inspected"
tester = "DDL desk research"
date = "2026-10-22"
engine_version = "0.30.1"
inspected = ["docs/research/reference-087-a.md §17–§20", "Archive, member, WAD lump, UMAPINFO and embedded DEHACKED inspection; 10x10/10x10.txt; coordinator-provided DoomWiki oldid=576470 identity; DSDA-Doom v0.30.1 source and release notes"]
notes = "Confirmed archive/member identities. The WAD has twelve map markers — MAP01–MAP10, the no-exit stopper MAP11 and the secret MAP31 — matching the readme's '11 (+1 no-exit stopper)' and the coordinator-provided DoomWiki page (12 map slots including ending and secret). It carries a 1,509-byte UMAPINFO, an embedded 490-byte DEHACKED [STRINGS] patch and 13 D_* music lumps, with no COMPLVL and no separate music WAD. The readme says Boom-compatible and tested DSDA-Doom 0.21.3, so family boom and complevel boom (9) follow the author and the Boom convention. The author describes the mapset as mapping exercises where he 'restricted myself to using ten stock textures and ten stock FLATs in each (with some universal textures such as switches, doors, DOORTRAK, lights, etc.)'; that ten-texture/ten-flat central constraint is the gimmick. Tags: cacowards = 2022 Cacowards Top Ten winner, https://www.doomworld.com/cacowards/2022/ (page not read live in this session; archived inventory docs/research/cacowards.md §2022); gimmick = the author's quoted ten-texture/ten-flat constraint, with the WAD/readme inspected here. megawad is not claimed (12 map slots is under 30), episode is not claimed (12 is over the nine-map limit), and classics is not claimed (2022 is under five years old). The author says pistol starts are intended, so the recipe sets the typed player-profile suggestion."
limitations = ["Needs Deck Validation: IWAD selection, complevel, UMAPINFO progression, embedded DEHACKED strings, load order, gameplay, audio and map selection.", "MAP11 'No Exit, It's Over' is a no-exit stopper (its UMAPINFO 'next' target MAP12 does not exist) and MAP31 'The Anna Dream' is the secret map; confirm the intended end and secret route on the Deck.", "The author's DoomWiki oldid=576470 page could not be read directly from this host (Cloudflare HTTP 403); its identity facts came from the coordinator's reading, while the archive/readme facts were inspected here."]
